speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have sudden-onset vertigo; to begin my assessment, how long have these dizzy spells been occurring, and is the spinning sensation continuous or does it come in episodes?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

The symptoms you described—a brief, sudden spinning sensation triggered by position change (going to bed), lasting only three minutes, followed by nausea and vomiting, with resolution to baseline—are classic for BPPV. Do you notice any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or drooping on one side of your face? REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver. REQUEST IMAGES: None required for this clinical assessment.
